_description: LLM model catalog with ratings and VRAM requirements. See README.md for schema.

models.name: Qwen 3 8B
models.blurb: Snappy 8B daily driver. Fine for chat; not an agent â€” fails multi-step tool loops in practice.

models.name: Llama 3.1 8B
models.blurb: Meta's stalwart 8B with 128 K context. Reliable for chat; do not expect agent reliability.

models.name: Phi-4 14B
models.blurb: Microsoft's 14 B is a math/reasoning specialist (~56 GPQA). Don't use it for agent loops.

models.name: Mistral Small 3 24B
models.blurb: Apache-licensed all-rounder. Sweet spot on a single 24 GB card; not viable for agentic work.

models.name: Gemma 3 27B
models.blurb: Google's vision-capable 27 B. Strong at OCR + chat; not an agent driver.

models.name: Qwen 3 32B
models.blurb: Strong general-purpose dense 32 B with thinking variant. Marginal agent â€” fails multi-step tool calls often.

models.name: Qwen 3 Coder 30B
models.blurb: Solid local coder for autocomplete + small-PR work. Now bracketed by Qwen 3.6-27B dense (better quality) and Qwen 3.6-35B-A3B MoE (better speed) â€” kept for users still on it.

models.name: Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B (MoE)
models.blurb: Apr 2026 release. 35B / 3B active MoE â€” beats Gemma 4-31B on agentic coding, matches Sonnet on most vision tasks. Native 262 K context (extensible to 1 M), ~18 GB at Q4. The new local-coding king under 200 B.

models.name: Qwen 3.6 27B (dense)
models.blurb: Apr 22 2026. Dense 27B that hits 77.2% SWE-Bench Verified â€” beats much larger MoEs on coding. Vision-capable, 262 K native context. Best single-24 GB-card coder right now.

models.name: Gemma 4 26B-A4B (MoE)
models.blurb: 26 B total / 4 B active MoE â€” fast and useful, but only 4 B 'thinking' caps reasoning + agent ceiling.

models.name: Qwen 3 Next 80B-A3B (MoE)
models.blurb: 80 B total, 3 B active per token. Faster than 30B-coder at similar quality. Decent agent in tight loops; struggles on long-horizon work.

models.name: Llama 3.3 70B
models.blurb: Solid local 70 B baseline for chat. Coding / agent quality lags Qwen-Coder, frontier MoEs, and closed models by a wide margin.

models.name: Llama 3.1 405B
models.blurb: Dense 405 B â€” heavy bandwidth need. Now eclipsed by DeepSeek V4-Pro, Kimi K2.6 and GLM-5.1 on every coding/agent benchmark; kept for chat-only setups with 256+ GB. Q2 fits in 2Ã— DGX Spark cluster or M3 Ultra 256.

models.name: DeepSeek R1 Distill 70B
models.blurb: Reasoning-distilled Llama 70 B. Best local 70 B for math/logic in early 2025; now lapped by Qwen 3.6-27B dense (better coding) and DeepSeek V4-Flash (better everything else).

models.name: GLM-4.5-Air 106B (MoE)
models.blurb: Zhipu's MoE 'Air' â€” ~38% on SWE-rebench, the strongest sub-200B agent model. Still 20+ pts behind frontier MoEs and closed models.

models.name: GLM-5.1 754B (MoE)
models.blurb: First open-weights model to top SWE-Bench Pro (April 2026). 8-hour autonomous coding agent. MIT.

models.name: GPT-OSS 120B
models.blurb: OpenAI's open-weights 120 B (MXFP4). ~33% SWE-rebench resolved. Strong all-rounder; agent ceiling is still frontier MoEs / closed models.

models.name: Mistral Medium 3.5 128B
models.blurb: Apr 30 2026. Western 128B dense with vision + 256 K context. 77.6% SWE-Bench Verified; first credible mid-tier open-weight from Mistral in months. Modified MIT.

models.name: MiniMax M2.7 230B-A10B (MoE)
models.blurb: Apr 12 2026. 230 B / 10 B active MoE â€” agent-tuned with native multi-agent ("Agent Teams"). 57% Terminal-Bench 2.0, 56% SWE-Bench Pro â€” strongest sub-300 B open-weights agent.

models.name: Tencent Hy3-preview 295B-A21B (MoE)
models.blurb: Apr 23 2026. Tencent's first major open-weight in months â€” 295 B / 21 B active MoE, 256 K context, 192 experts. ~74% SWE-Bench Verified. Custom non-MIT Tencent Hy license.

models.name: Qwen 3 235B-A22B (MoE)
models.blurb: Excellent reasoning + chat. Strong coding too â€” but coding SOTA is GLM-5.1 / DeepSeek V3 / Kimi K2.

models.name: Kimi K2 1T (MoE)
models.blurb: Original 1 T MoE â€” superseded by K2.5 / K2.6 for agents. Q2_K_XL ~250 GB fits 4Ã— DGX Spark or M3 Ultra 512 GB.

models.name: Kimi K2.5 1T (MoE)
models.blurb: Same architecture as K2; long-horizon agent training + native image input. Strong open-weights agent â€” close to closed frontier.

models.name: Kimi K2.6 1T (MoE)
models.blurb: Apr 2026 release. 66.7% Terminal-Bench 2.0 â€” top open-weights agent. Native INT4, 262 K context, native image + video input.

models.name: DeepSeek V3 671B (MoE)
models.blurb: 671 B MoE â€” superseded by V4 for agents. Q2 (~220 GB) fits 4Ã— DGX Spark; Q4 needs 512 GB / 8Ã—H100.

models.name: DeepSeek V4-Flash 284B (MoE)
models.blurb: Apr 2026 release. 284 B / 13 B active, 1 M-token context. ~57% Terminal-Bench. The agent-grade DeepSeek that fits a single Pro 6000 build.

models.name: DeepSeek V4-Pro 1.6T (MoE)
models.blurb: Apr 2026 release. 1.6 T / 49 B active, 1 M-token context. 67.9% Terminal-Bench â€” top open-weights agent, matches closed frontier on most agentic tasks. Q2 ~430 GB.

models.name: SDXL 1.0
models.blurb: Legacy 3.5 B SDXL â€” runs on 8 GB, huge LoRA ecosystem. Beat by FLUX on prompt + photorealism.

models.name: Z-Image-Turbo
models.blurb: Apache-2.0 turbo model â€” very fast, decent quality, fits 8 GB cards. Smaller community vs SD/FLUX.

models.name: FLUX.1 [schnell]
models.blurb: Apache-2.0 distilled FLUX, 4-step generation. Best fast permissive option for commercial use.

models.name: FLUX.1 [dev]
models.blurb: The 2026 photorealism crown â€” best lighting, anatomy, text rendering. Non-commercial; commercial license $$.

models.name: FLUX.2 [klein]
models.blurb: FLUX.2 small variant â€” strong prompt-following at SD-class VRAM. Commercial license required.

models.name: FLUX.2 [dev]
models.blurb: Black Forest Labs' 2026 flagship. Better prompt + style than FLUX.1 [dev], same VRAM footprint.

models.name: Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large
models.blurb: Stability's 2024-2026 flagship. Strong style versatility, mature ecosystem (ControlNet, IP-Adapter).

models.name: Qwen-Image (Alibaba)
models.blurb: Apache-2.0 â€” best-in-class for in-image text rendering (English + Chinese), strong style range.

models.name: HiDream-I1 (Full)
models.blurb: MIT-licensed 17 B â€” competes with FLUX.1 [dev] on quality without commercial restrictions. Superseded by HiDream-O1-Image (May 2026) on prompt alignment and arena rank.

models.name: HiDream-O1-Image
models.blurb: May 8 2026. 8 B MIT-licensed pixel-space unified transformer (no VAE, no separate text encoder). GenEval 0.90 / DPG 89.83 â€” debuted at #8 on AA arena, highest-ranked open-weights image model. 2048Ã—2048 native.

models.name: LTX-Video 2B
models.blurb: Real-time-ish on a 4090 â€” 5 s 720p clip in ~90 s. Fastest open video model; quality below WAN/Hunyuan.

models.name: WAN 2.1 1.3B
models.blurb: Smallest open video model â€” 8 GB VRAM, 480p. The 'video on a laptop GPU' option.

models.name: WAN 2.2 14B (MoE)
models.blurb: MoE: high-noise + low-noise experts. 5 s 720p in ~3-5 min on a 5090; GGUF quants run on 12 GB.

models.name: WAN 2.5 14B
models.blurb: VRAM-hungry but produces 1080p. 16 GB tile-mode possible with WanGP optimizations.

models.name: HunyuanVideo 1.5
models.blurb: Trimmed to 8.3 B and 14 GB w/ offload. Better instruction-following + structural stability than WAN 2.2.

models.name: HunyuanVideo 13B (original)
models.blurb: Original 13 B â€” best motion realism among open weights. 60-80 GB VRAM at full quality (datacenter).

models.name: Mochi 1
models.blurb: Permissive + capable, but slower than WAN 2.2. ~8 min for 5 s clip on a 4090.
